Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both required 3D wake views—and consult the fish-control bookshelf before proposing the single candidate. I’ll keep all changes confined to this Phase 2 workspace and update both required notes files.

The workspace confirms the candidate must remain continuously valid, that no CFD should be run here, and that the provenance note must precede the policy edit. I’m now applying the two workspace skills: the bookshelf skill will constrain mechanism transfer to normalized body-frame feedback, and the visual-evidence skill requires inspecting both wake views before any policy change.

`rg` is unavailable in this workspace, so I’m using a read-only file inventory to locate every available rollout artifact and inherited log. There appears to be one sampled solver in the README; I’ll determine whether the inherited optimizer material contains a second comparison trajectory or whether the evidence set genuinely has only the seed failure.

The visual and metric evidence agree: this is genuine self-propulsion in direct still water, with a coherent alternating wake and strong initial progress, not advection. The failure is directional: after reaching 4.780 L, the fish continues curving toward the lower boundary and exits at 27.49 T while distance regresses to 9.709 L. Because only this seed rollout is sampled, it is simultaneously the strongest finite trajectory and the informative failure; there is no second solver result to compare. I’m now consulting the bookshelf references to select one compact corrective mechanism, as required before the first architecture proposal.

The evidence supports a mechanism change, not propulsion retuning: the seed’s joints already reach 27.5°/36.3° and both hit the 260°/T velocity cap, while the coherent wake remains propulsive. I’ll test one state-triggered C-bend redirect: large normalized body-frame bearing will smoothly shift the oscillator’s centerline into same-sign anterior/posterior curvature and reduce oscillatory amplitude until alignment returns. The expected effect is an earlier course reversal without adding time, route, or world-coordinate dependence.

The candidate and durable lesson are now both updated. The edit preserves the successful traveling-wave carrier and changes only the large-error steering topology; the guidance records the evidence boundary explicitly so this unevaluated candidate is not mistaken for a proven improvement. I’m checking parameter ownership, syntax, symmetry/bounds, and representative state responses before invoking the required checker.

The first required guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace inconsistency before assessing my edit: `README.md` lists the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker reports “found 2” where it requires exactly one. I’m inspecting that checker and the parent markers now; I’ll make only the smallest in-workspace repair needed, without touching solver surfaces outside the authorized candidate.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated parent marker. The policy check itself is blocked by the environment—not the candidate: this container has no `julia` executable on `PATH` (the standalone policy was therefore not evaluated). I’m checking for an alternate Julia installation, then I’ll run the remaining deterministic boundary/schema checks and invoke the configured checker for an independent verdict.

The configured checker agent could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported by this account. That is an execution-environment failure before any check ran. I’ve already reproduced its guidance and boundary checks locally; I’m invoking an available checker agent against the same TOML command set so the final audit is still independent, with the missing Julia runtime called out separately.

The independent fallback audit agrees with the local results: guidance provenance PASS, boundary PASS, and all 54 referenced parameter fields are owned by the 56-field parameter object. No CFD ran. The only unavailable check is Julia execution because this workspace image contains no Julia binary; delimiter/function structure passed a lightweight static audit, but I won’t present that as a Julia parse.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1). It preserves the propulsive traveling wave and adds a body-frame-error-gated C-bend redirect with temporary amplitude/lag relief.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1), including the required bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:25) with an evidence-backed reusable lesson.
- De-duplicated the assigned-parent marker in [README.md](README.md:102) so the required checker could run.

Validation:

- Guidance/provenance: PASS
- Solver boundary: PASS
- Parameter-schema audit: PASS
- Julia contract execution: unavailable because `julia` is not installed; static structure checks passed
- CFD: not run, as required
